_README: One variable: tire pressure, 31.5 -> 50.0 psi both ends, on the app's tune.
Everything else held. Taken to test the last remaining candidate for the
gearing axis; it eliminated that candidate and produced three findings
about other things, which is the usual return on a clean single-variable
screen: tuning menu — TIRES and GEARING tabs
axisEliminated: TIRE PRESSURE DOES NOT MOVE THE AXIS. 31.5 -> 50.0 psi, a 59% change and
the most plausible remaining lever on rolling radius, and the axis held at
159 with the midpoint label at 79.
EVERY TUNE-SIDE CANDIDATE IS NOW DEAD:
final drive       held 157 across 3.50-4.60
top gear ratio    0.85 -> 0.75 -> 0.85, no change
aero              0.743 reads 159 while 0.741 read 157
tire pressure     31.5 -> 50.0, no change
And every tune we can reproduce — the game's default, the default with a
moved 7th, a freshly generated app tune, and that tune at 50 psi — reads
159. The only 157 ever recorded on this car came from the tune that was
already on it this morning, which was replaced before its settings were
captured and cannot be reconstructed.
THE HONEST POSITION: the axis is 159 for this build, and the single 157 is
unreproducible. It is not being called a misreading — Boston's standing
observation is that PARTS move it, and no part has changed all day, so
there is no mechanism on the table that explains it either. It is recorded
as unexplained.
THIS INVERTS THIS MORNING'S E2 ARGUMENT, and that is worth stating
plainly. The k = 588.3 that made 157 'the reading that survives' was built
from a fit of 4.57 read on the tune that showed 157. Internally consistent,
but it is one tune's pair, and the axis on every reproducible tune of this
build is the value gearing.test.js uses, not the one sweep.test.js uses.
WHAT SETTLES IT CHEAPLY: re-read the fit NOW, on this tune. The app's
ratios are applied, so the top gear really is 0.82 and for the first time
the axis, the fit and the gearbox all belong to the same setup. That gives
a k that is not assembled from two different tunes, and it can be compared
against 588.3 directly.
mbRespondsToPressure: MECHANICAL BALANCE MOVED WITH NOTHING BUT TIRE PRESSURE: 0.51 -> 0.50.
Bars, springs and ride height were all untouched. No candidate model in
MEASURE.md Phase 1 — M1 through M5 — contains a tire term at all.
Physically it is reasonable: tire vertical stiffness sits in series with
the spring and the bar in the roll-stiffness chain, and pressure changes
it. What is odd is that pressure moved EQUALLY at both ends and the
balance still shifted, which means the two axles are not contributing
symmetrically — different loads, or different effective rates.
SIZE AND CAVEAT: 0.01 on a 2-decimal readout, so it could be as little as
a rounding boundary crossing (0.505 -> 0.504). It is one step, in a
sitting where the panel has been shown deterministic, so it is real — but
it is one step, and the pressure change was enormous. The effect is small.
WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE MB SWEEP: pressure must be HELD and RECORDED on
every row of Phase 1, which the balance template does not currently ask
for. A sweep that let pressure drift would blame the bars for a tire
brakingAndGrip: TWO RESULTS THAT HAVE NOTHING TO DO WITH WHY THE ROW WAS TAKEN.
1. BRAKING IMPROVED SHARPLY WITH PRESSURE. 60-0 went 68.4 -> 65.7 ft and
100-0 went 153.1 -> 150.6 ft, so 2.7 ft and 2.5 ft better at 50 psi.
That is half the gap to the game's default tune (63.2 ft) recovered by
one slider the app sets from a fixed table: PSI.semi = 31 in
index.html:523, which is where the app's 31.5 came from.
The app's pressures are a per-compound constant with no per-car or
per-discipline term, and on this car the panel says higher is better for
stopping. Not actionable yet — panel braking is straight-line only and
cannot see what pressure does to tire temperature over a stint, which is
the whole reason a pressure target exists (case T1). But it is a
measurable column where the app's constant is not the optimum.
2. LATERAL G DID NOT MOVE AT ALL. 1.26 and 1.42 at both speeds, across a
59% pressure change. Case S5 asks whether lateral G responds to the tune
or is essentially a compound readout; this is the first evidence and it
points at compound. If camber and bars also leave it flat, S5's hoped-for
promotion of grip constants from lap-times-only to panel-measurable does
not happen, and that is worth knowing before designing an hour of it.
It also makes lateral G a clean CONTROL: it is now known not to respond
to gearing or to pressure, so if it moves in some later row, whatever
moved is worth looking at.
notes: 0-100 got slightly worse with pressure (8.883 -> 8.933, three frames) and top speed fell 0.3 mph, both consistent with less grip on launch and marginally more rolling resistance or a smaller contact patch. 0-60 did not move at all, which is the frame-quantised column being too coarse to show a small effect: at 1/60 s resolution a change under 0.017 s is invisible, so 0-60 flat does not mean 0-60 unaffected.
